children: By Emily Ou Yong
Iron ore futures fell on Tuesday, as ample global supply, elevated Chinese port inventories, and declining shipping costs weighed on prices.
The most-traded January iron ore contract on China's Dalian Commodity Exchange (DCE)
traded 0.58% lower at 680.5 yuan ($101.64) a metric ton, as of 0313 GMT.
The benchmark November iron ore (SZZFX6) on the Singapore Exchange was 0.31% lower at $90.65 a ton.
Iron ore inventory at major Chinese ports rose 0.19% week-on-week to 152.66 million tons as of Friday, data from consultancy Steelhome showed.

Supply remains comfortable despite a slight tightening, while increased blast furnace maintenance after the holiday continues to weigh on near-term demand, analysts from Shanghai Metals Market said in a note.

The first round of coke price cuts has improved steel mill margins, but soft end-user demand has so far limited any increase in iron ore purchases, the analysts said, adding that ore prices were likely to remain rangebound at relatively low levels in the near term.
Major steel mills in China's Shandong and Hebei provinces lowered coking coal purchase prices on Monday, completing a second round of coking coal price reductions, according to consultancy Mysteel.

Declining shipping costs have weakened cost support for iron ore since the Golden Week holiday, leaving the ore market under pressure, Xu Yanyan, analyst at broker Chaos Tianfeng Futures, said in a note.
The Capesize C5 route from Australia to China fell $0.64 a ton and the C3 route from Brazil to China fell $0.37 a ton on Monday, Mysteel data showed.

Elsewhere, global steel demand is expected to shrink 0.1% in 2026, reversing an April forecast for 0.3% growth, the World Steel Association said on Monday, citing weaker demand in China and disruption from the US-Iran conflict.
Other steelmaking ingredients on the DCE were mixed, with coking coal
NYMEX:ACT1!
up 0.55% and coke (DCJcv1) down 0.15%.
Steel benchmarks on the Shanghai Futures Exchange lost ground. Rebar
fell 0.32%, hot-rolled coil
lost 0.31% and stainless steel
declined 0.59%.
($1 = 6.6951 Chinese yuan)
